title: PRO-NANO-OTT: A prospective feasibility study of the implementation of a structured neuro-oncology assessment pathway and the evaluation of oncology exercise therapy in patients with central nervous system tumours
summary:
People with a brain tumour or with cancer that has spread to the brain often experience severe tiredness, feel unsteady when walking or find everyday activities difficult. Some are advised to take part in an exercise programme tailored to their needs. This study looks at how well the hospital and the exercise team can work together to support them. We want to find out how many people start and complete the recommended programme, what difficulties they encounter and how their symptoms and independence change during this time.

Before starting exercise and at a later hospital appointment, participants answer questions about tiredness and quality of life. The clinical team also assesses how safely they can move around and how independently they manage daily activities. The exercise team records which sessions they attend, how they manage the exercises and whether symptoms or falls occur. Patients and their care teams decide on exercise therapy independently of participation in this study.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified sites

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Confirmed neuro-oncological disease, particularly brain metastases, high- or low-grade gliomas, or other primary or secondary central nervous system tumours.
• Presentation at the neuro-oncology or neurosurgery outpatient clinic of University Hospital Düsseldorf.
• Medical recommendation for, or planned initiation of, an oncology exercise therapy programme (OTT).
• Sufficient cognitive and clinical capacity to participate in the baseline assessments.
• Capacity to provide informed consent and written informed consent to study participation.
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute clinical instability currently precluding participation in oncology exercise therapy.
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent without legally valid representation.
• Severe intercurrent illness rendering participation in the assessments or oncology exercise therapy impracticable.
• Lack of organisational feasibility of the planned care pathway.
• Refusal to participate in the study.
